# 1 Maccabees Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_001_page_001.jpg

---

1. After Alexander son of Philip the Macedonian, who came forth from the land of Kittim, had defeated Darius king of the Persians and Medes, he reigned in his place, having previously reigned over Greece.
2. He fought many battles, captured strongholds, and put to death kings of the earth.
3. He advanced to the ends of the earth and plundered many nations. The earth grew quiet before him, and his heart was lifted up in pride.
4. He assembled a very strong army and ruled over provinces, nations, and princes, and they became his tributaries.
5. Afterwards he fell ill and knew that he was dying.
6. He summoned his most honored officers, men who had been brought up with him from his youth, and while he was still alive he distributed his kingdom among them.
7. Alexander had reigned twelve years when he died.
8. His officers took control, each in his own region.
9. After his death they all assumed the royal crown, as did their descendants after them for many years; and they multiplied evils in the earth.
10. From among them there emerged a sinful offshoot — Antiochus Epiphanes, son of King Antiochus, formerly a hostage at Rome — who became king in the one hundred and thirty-seventh year of the Greek kingdom.
11. In those days there went out from Israel certain lawless men who persuaded many, saying, "Let us go and make a covenant with the Gentiles around us, for ever since we separated from them we have encountered much trouble."
12. This proposal seemed good to them.
13. Some of the people went eagerly to the king, and he authorized them to follow the ordinances of the Gentiles.
14. They built a gymnasium in Jerusalem according to the customs of the Gentiles,
15. had themselves uncircumcised, abandoned the holy covenant, joined themselves to the Gentiles, and sold themselves to do evil.
16. When his kingdom was firmly established before him, Antiochus determined to become king over Egypt, so that he might rule over both kingdoms.
17. He invaded Egypt with a strong force — with chariots, war elephants, cavalry, and a great fleet —
18. and made war against Ptolemy king of Egypt. Ptolemy turned and fled before him, and many were wounded and fell.
19. He captured the fortified cities of Egypt and plundered all the land of Egypt.
20. Antiochus turned back after his conquest of Egypt, in the one hundred and forty-third year, and marched against Israel and Jerusalem with a strong force.
21. In his arrogance he entered the sanctuary and took the golden altar, the lampstand with all its equipment,
22. the table of the bread of the Presence, the libation vessels, the cups, the golden censers, the curtain, the crowns, and the golden decoration on the facade of the temple — he stripped it all off.
23. He took the silver and the gold and the precious vessels; he took also the hidden treasures that he found.
24. Taking everything, he departed to his own land. He had shed much blood and spoke with great arrogance.
25. There was great mourning throughout all Israel, in every place.
26. Rulers and elders groaned; virgins and young men grew faint; the beauty of the women was altered.
27. Every bridegroom took up a lament; she who sat in the bridal chamber was in grief.
28. The earth trembled on behalf of its inhabitants, and all the house of Jacob was clothed in shame.
29. Two full years later the king sent a chief collector of tribute to the cities of Judah, and he came to Jerusalem with a large force.
30. He spoke peaceful words to them in deceit, and they trusted him. Then he suddenly fell upon the city, struck it severely, and destroyed many people of Israel.
31. He plundered the city and burned it with fire, tore down its houses and surrounding walls.
32. They took captive the women and children, and seized the cattle.
33. Then they fortified the city of David with a great strong wall and strong towers, and it became their citadel.
34. They stationed there a sinful people, lawless men; and these garrisoned it.
35. They stored arms and provisions in it, and collected there the plunder of Jerusalem; and it became a grave danger.
36. It became an ambush against the sanctuary, and a constant evil adversary to Israel.
37. They shed innocent blood on every side of the sanctuary; they defiled the sanctuary.
38. Because of them the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled; it became a habitation for strangers. It became alien to those born in it, and its own children forsook it.
39. Its sanctuary became desolate like a wilderness; its feasts were turned to mourning, its sabbaths to shame, its honor to contempt.
40. In proportion to its former glory, so was its dishonor multiplied; its high estate was turned to grief.
41. Then the king issued a decree throughout his entire kingdom that all peoples should become one,
42. each abandoning his particular customs.
43. All the Gentiles accepted the conditions of the king's decree. Many in Israel also willingly accepted his religion; they sacrificed to idols and profaned the sabbath.
44. The king sent letters by messengers to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, ordering them to follow practices foreign to their land:
45. to prohibit burnt offerings, sacrifices, and drink offerings in the sanctuary; to profane sabbaths and festivals;
46. to defile the sanctuary and the holy people;
47. to erect altars, sacred groves, and idolatrous shrines; to sacrifice pigs and other unclean animals;
48. to leave their sons uncircumcised; and to make themselves abominable with every kind of uncleanness and profanation,
49. so that they would forget the Torah and change all their ordinances.
50. Whoever did not comply with the king's command would die.
51. In accordance with all that he had written, he appointed inspectors over all the people and commanded the cities of Judah to offer sacrifice, one city after another.
52. Many of the people, all who had abandoned the Torah, joined them and did evil in the land.
53. They drove Israel into hiding in every place of refuge.
54. On the fifteenth day of Chislev, in the one hundred and forty-fifth year, they set up a desolating abomination upon the altar of burnt offerings; and they built altars throughout the cities of Judah on every side.
55. They burned incense at the doors of houses and in the streets.
56. They tore to pieces and burned with fire the scrolls of the Torah that they found.
57. Anyone with whom a scroll of the covenant was found, or who observed the Torah, the king's decree condemned to death.
58. Month after month they dealt violently with every Israelite found in the cities.
59. On the twenty-fifth day of the month they offered sacrifice on the illicit altar that was built over the altar of burnt offerings.
60. According to the decree they put to death the women who had circumcised their children,
61. hanging the infants from their mothers' necks; they put to death also their families and those who had performed the circumcisions.
62. Yet many in Israel stood firm and resolved in their hearts not to eat unclean food.
63. They preferred to die rather than to be defiled by food or to profane the holy covenant; and they did die.
64. And very great wrath fell upon Israel.
